newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia TSUM sets 2,000 rbl share price.
newsitem.headline: Russia TSUM sets 2,000 rbl share price.

text.p: Russia's AO Torgovy Dom TSUM retailer set the price of its forthcoming issue of shares at 2,000 roubles a share, lead manager IK OLMA said on Monday.
TSUM plans to sell 30 million shares from October 1 to December 31, 1996, to cover part of a $22 million reconstruction project, OLMA president Oleg Yachnik told a news conference.
The issue would raise 60 billion roubles (about $12 million) for the project.
The rest will be covered from TSUM's cash flow and by bank loans.
The project will increase floor space at TSUM's central Moscow store by 60 percent from the current 9,300 square meters, TSUM general manager Alexander Voskoboinikov told the news conference.
At 1245 GMT TSUM was traded at $0.360 after $0.335 at Friday's close.
Yachnik said OLMA already had preliminary bids for between 60 to 70 percent of the new issue. Between five to seven percent of the issue will be allocated to households, he said.
The agent for the placement will be Banque Societe Generale Vostok, a subsidiary of France's Societe Generale, Yachnik said.
TSUM had a profit before tax of 21.14 billion roubles in 1995 on sales of 53.46 billion.

The Moscow city government is TSUM's biggest shareholder with 24.50 percent stake, Swiss private bank Pictet & Cie has 6.71 percent, OLMA-Bank has 5.03 percent and AOOT Russ-Invest, a Russian investment fund, has about 5.5 percent.
